messages:
raj_sales: Heads up — Nimbus POC reporting inconsistent latency. TTFT sometimes 600-900ms, other times ~80ms. They say it correlates with spikes in small requests.

ops_ryan: Which deployment? Hosted or Dedicated?

raj_sales: Dedicated in their VPC peered subnet. They run a webhook fanout that sends lots of tiny prompts in parallel.

sre_emma: Classic micro-batching problem. If client sends many 1-token requests, server batching may wait for window to fill -> higher per-request latency. Do we have batch window metrics for their pool?

infra-bot: metric: pool=nimbus-dedicated | batch_window_ms.p50=12 | p95=120 | avg_batch_size=3 at 2026-03-05T09:40Z.

ops_ryan: avg_batch_size=3 seems ok but p95 window 120ms is high. Are they using our default batch_timeout or a route override?

pm_julia: They used an internal integration that sets `interactive=true` on requests (which disables server-side batching in our runtime). But they say they didn't set it intentionally  could be SDK mismatch.

sre_emma: If interactive=true, then those requests bypass batching and hit single-token path -> lower throughput but lower batching wait time. That wouldn't explain spikes to 900ms though.

raj_sales: Attached customer timeline shows spikes when they simultaneously run a background job that calls the model for short summaries and their frontend traffic spikes.

ops_ryan: Two hypotheses: 1) Cold KV/cache misses when different prompt prefixes are used by background job vs frontend, 2) Head-of-line blocking in the request queue due to large streaming responses occupying worker slots.

infra-bot: alert: pool=nimbus-dedicated worker-util=92% at 2026-03-05T09:42:01Z.

sre_emma: Worker util 92% is a smoking gun. If workers are saturated, small requests queue behind streaming responses and see high TTFT. Check per-worker concurrent streams limit.

pm_julia: They configured max_concurrency per worker to 2 in their Dedicated profile to preserve predictability (they wanted low tail latency for long jobs). That may be too low for mixed workloads.

security_ben: Also saw a handful of 503 gateway_timeout for streaming connections around the same window. Customer proxy may be dropping long streams causing retries.

ops_ryan: Proposed triage steps: 1) temporarily increase per-worker concurrency to 4 for the pool, 2) enable request-priority preemption for short requests, 3) increase prefix cache TTL for summary prompts, 4) ask customer to mark background jobs with a lower priority tag.

raj_sales: Customer agreed to try changes during a 1hr window. Emma/ryan can you put exact flags and a rollback plan?

sre_emma: Flags: `worker.defaults.max_concurrency=4` (control-plane). Priority: set `route.nimbus-prod.priority_map={"short": 10, "default": 5, "long": 1}` and clients should set `x-request-priority: short` for quick prompts. Prefix TTL: `model.gpt-lite.prefix_ttl=45s` (was 5s). Rollback: revert concurrency and priority within 60m if error rate increases.

ops_ryan: Implemented concurrency bump. Observing median TTFT drop 610ms -> 95ms within 90s. Worker util down to 68%.

raj_sales: Customer reports frontend latency improved. Background jobs still sometimes cause small spikes.

pm_julia: We recommended adding a small jitter to their retry logic and reducing streaming response sizes (chunk smaller). Also suggested they enable connection pooling via our SDK to reduce TCP churn.

security_ben: Approved temporary control-plane changes. Please capture audit trail and revert after the test window.

ops_ryan: Monitoring link: https://console.redwood.example/obs/pool/nimbus-dedicated?from=2026-03-05T09:30Z. Sampling traces: enabled `trace.sample=1%` for the pool.

raj_sales: Customer asked about pricing impact of concurrency bump and higher cache TTL during POC. Any notes?

sre_emma: Cost: concurrency bump increases instantaneous GPU utilization but falls back when idle. Recommend billing note to customer: "Short term bump may increase usage-based charges; we'll track delta and revert after POC."

raj_sales: Action items recap:
raj_sales: - ops_ryan: revert concurrency and priorities after 60m if stable
raj_sales: - sre_emma: keep prefix_ttl change for POC, monitor cache hit rate
raj_sales: - pm_julia: send integrator checklist (use SDK, set priority header, avoid large streaming in foreground)
raj_sales: - security_ben: confirm audit logs retained

infra-bot: deploy: applied worker.defaults.max_concurrency=4 to pool=nimbus-dedicated at 2026-03-05T09:44:12Z.

raj_sales: Check-in in 45m. Thanks all. :rocket:
